title: China-to-Chile Lithium Battery & Power Bank Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Electrical Product Approval Path — SEC Marking Scope
rows.target_requirement: In Chile, SEC regulates electrical products and requires in-scope products to follow SEC approval and marking rules using authorized certifiers. The SEC seal is a market-access signal expected where electrical safety or related energy-safety scope applies.
target_standards: SEC Chile official approval framework for electrical products
INN NCh standards ecosystem aligned to IEC references for product classes under SEC scope
Authorized certification body and mark-issuance requirements in SEC channels
rows.china_equivalent: China-side requirements are framed through CCC where applicable and GB/GB T product safety standards. These are relevant technical inputs but are not accepted as a Chilean SEC market clearance substitute.
china_standards: China Compulsory Certification (CCC) where required by product category
GB 31241 safety specification and related GB/GB T supporting standards
China factory, test report, and compliance documentation model for exports
rows.gap: The exporter gap is that SEC scope clearance is treated as the Chile-specific admissibility gate, while China docs usually stop at Chinese conformity. Prepare SEC-facing documentation from the Chile importer side and do not treat CCC or GB/T reports as Chile approvals.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where SEC scope applies to the product model before commercialization in Chile.
mandatory_status.cn: CCC/GB documentation is mandatory or relevant on China-side manufacture, but not equivalent to SEC market clearance.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat SEC participation and mark requirements as target-market obligations that cannot be fulfilled by Chinese domestic conformity documents alone.

source.publisher: Superintendencia de Electricidad y Combustibles (SEC), Government of Chile

rows.target_requirement: Lithium battery and power bank suppliers entering Chile should map the product to NCh-adopted IEC 62133 safety expectations, including abuse and protection performance for lithium cells and packs, because Chilean market review has been moving toward standards-based safety evidence for import.
target_standards: INN NCh-aligned battery safety standards based on IEC 62133
SEC electrical product safety handling rules for lithium battery-containing devices
Industry practice references for lithium battery safety test dossiers linked to IEC criteria
rows.china_equivalent: China uses GB 31241 and related GB/GB T safety standards for lithium battery construction and testing. Those are valid Chinese baselines, but they are not a full substitute for Chile-adapted NCh expectations under SEC review.
china_standards: GB / GB T lithium-cell and battery testing standards
CCC electrical safety records used for China compliance
rows.gap: Chinese reports are helpful but may not be accepted as-is for Chilean battery-safety review. A Chile-facing file should identify the exact battery chemistry, capacity band, cell format, and safety test scope, and then evidence compatibility with NCh/IEC 62133 expectations.

mandatory_status.target: Typically mandatory where lithium battery cells and packs are in scope of SEC-administrable electrical product safety expectations.
mandatory_status.cn: GB/GB T safety testing is mandatory or expected in China for domestic compliance, but not treated as Chile approval.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Use Chinese GB/GB T test results as baseline material, then reframe into Chile-targeted product documentation for NCh/IEC alignment.

source.publisher: Government of Chile portal (linking to INN/SEC related standards context)

rows.target_requirement: Chile does not have a single EU-style horizontal regime equivalent to CE marking, RoHS, or a dedicated Chile-wide battery regulation in the same form. For products with radio functions, SUBTEL approval is the practical regime to check, while SEC and related sector rules still govern in-scope electrical aspects.
target_standards: Telecommunications and radio compliance practice under SUBTEL
NCh-referenced EMC and safety alignment expected by market actors
No Chile-specific standalone national RoHS or battery regulation equivalent is broadly cited in this lane
rows.china_equivalent: China may document EMI/EMC and radio compliance under GB and GB/T routes tied to product category and market destination, and CCC where applicable. These records remain Chinese-side records unless mapped to Chilean requirements.
china_standards: China GB 9254 safety-related EMC practice where relevant
GB 9258 radio-related test expectations by category
CCC / GB T compliance dossier when applicable for exported battery products
rows.gap: Do not assume CE, RoHS, or one EMC label transfer applies for Chile. The exporter gap is usually claim control and module scope: no EU-style umbrella claim is accepted without Chile-specific evidence for the exact wireless and electrical profile.

mandatory_status.target: Depends on radio/function scope; no blanket EU-style CE/ROHS-style umbrella applies by default to all products.
mandatory_status.cn: China-side EMC and radio documentation is required by category but not a direct Chile exemption framework.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Avoid EU-style all-products statements. Validate SEC, and where wireless is present, SUBTEL-facing tests and claims for Chile import models.

source.publisher: Subsecretaría de Telecomunicaciones (SUBTEL), Government of Chile

rows.requirement: Market Access Architecture — Importer-led Chile Entry
rows.target_requirement: Chile market entry for lithium batteries and power banks is not a single certifier shortcut. Importers are central, ports commonly used include Valparaiso and San Antonio, and relevant evidence may combine SEC compliance path, energy labelling checks, and occupational safety obligations in the workplace chain through ISP-aligned practices.
target_standards: SEC electrical market-access compliance expectations for imported equipment
Chile energy-efficiency labeling context for applicable electrical products
ISP occupational safety responsibility model for importers and handlers in production and storage chains
rows.china_equivalent: China export files often combine GB/GB T safety evidence, manufacturer declaration packages, and logistic documents. That is useful background evidence but does not replace Chile importer-led market-access responsibilities.
china_standards: GB / GB T safety documentation requirements in China
CCC and related China market documentation channels
Export paperwork models used for customs and shipping to Latin America
rows.gap: The gap is organizational, not only technical. Chinese commercial packets are often built for shipment and China customs, while Chile requires a Chile importer, labeling model, and port entry control trail that match Chile requirements. Clarify responsibility for compliance claims before finalizing sales terms.

mandatory_status.target: No single umbrella mark; imported lithium battery products are evaluated through multiple entry controls and the local importer role.
mandatory_status.cn: China-side documentation is mandatory for China manufacturing/export logistics but does not complete Chile market access.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Build a Chile-specific entry checklist that includes importer responsibility, labeling model, port-entry flow, and safety documentation, not a single export packet fallback.

source.publisher: Ministry of Energy, Government of Chile

rows.requirement: Transport — UN 38.3 and Chile Import Logistics
rows.target_requirement: Lithium batteries and power banks must be handled as dangerous goods for transport planning and documentation, with UN 38.3 evidence for the model and packaging, including port and carrier acceptance conditions at likely Chile entry ports such as Valparaiso and San Antonio.
target_standards: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III, Section 38.3
UN model dangerous-goods transport framework used by air and sea carriers
Chile logistics acceptance and customs documentary checks at entry ports
rows.china_equivalent: China exporters usually maintain UN 38.3 test reports, SDS/MSDS, and transport pack documentation. These are necessary for outbound logistics and often reused, but they are only the base layer of Chile-bound transport compliance.
china_standards: China GB 1948 hazard logistics and dangerous goods support documents
UN 38.3 report model used for export shipments
Air and sea freight dangerous goods documentation rules used by freight forwarders
rows.gap: The exporter gap is that UN 38.3 documents are model-specific and can become non-compliant if chemistry, cell format, or packaging design changes. Chile-bound shipments additionally need carrier/port checks and importer coordination at Chile logistics nodes.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for lithium battery logistics; transport evidence is essential for dangerous-goods handling and port acceptance.
mandatory_status.cn: Dangerous-goods logistics documentation is commonly mandatory for China exporters and remains essential for Chile-bound goods as baseline evidence.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] A UN 38.3 report remains necessary for lithium products, but Chile entry still depends on port logistics controls and importer-side dangerous-goods handling readiness.

source.publisher: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE), UN Manual of Tests and Criteria
